raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

#42465: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK` and HiCache `write_through` deadlocks across TP ranks. With `SGLANG_ENABLE_RANK_CONSENSUS_CHECKER=1` the ranks diverge on `cache_finished_req ... owned_kv_len` by 1-2 tokens, so each rank inserts a different prefix and the write-through backups no longer line up.

The mechanism, as @divyvasal found: the folded accept runs inside the target-verify CUDA graph and writes fixed epilogue buffers (`commit_lens_buf`, `out_tokens_buf`, ...) that the next replay rewrites. `accept_and_finalize(folded_accept=True)` returned `read_accept(bs)`, i.e. views of those buffers, and the DSPARK worker put them into `GenerationBatchResult.accept_lens` / `next_token_ids`. Under the overlap scheduler `_copy_result_to_cpu` issues that readback on `copy_stream` after `copy_stream.wait_stream(forward_stream)` and then launches forward N+1 without waiting for the copy. When the copy engine is busy, for example behind the write-through device-to-host copy of a ~540K-token prefix, the readback runs after replay N+1 and reads step N+1's accept lengths. Each rank races on its own, so ranks commit different token counts. The in-graph accept is broadcast from rank 0, so the ranks agree on the device; only the host readback diverges.

## Modifications

- `dspark_verify.py`: `DsparkVerifyEpilogue.snapshot_accept(bs)` returns clones of the six accept buffers. The clones are made on the forward stream right after the replay, so stream order pins them to step N, and `async_d2h`'s `record_stream` keeps them alive until the readback has run. `TargetVerifyExecutor.accept_and_finalize` returns the snapshot on the folded path. `read_accept` keeps returning views, because the in-graph `_accept` writes through them (`build_accept_outs(..., out=self.read_accept(bs))`).
- `scheduler.py`: comment in `_copy_result_to_cpu` updated; no behavior change (the DSpark inline copy under Confidential Computing is kept as validated).
- Cost: six small device-to-device copies per verify step on the forward stream, no extra stream sync.

### Relation to #42812

#42812 clones inside `read_accept`. That was right at its base (264d1c20, 2026-10-06), where `_accept` wrote the buffers directly. Since #43790 (2026-10-12) `_accept` passes `read_accept(bs)` as its in-graph destination, so cloning there makes the graph write into throwaway clones and the static buffers never update. On today's main the existing `test_dspark_accept_tail.py::test_graph_accept_matches_eager_greedy` fails with #42812's hunk applied (4 subtests). This PR keeps the alias where the graph needs it and snapshots where the views escape. @shanemort1982 reported the same breakage on #42812 on 2026-10-19 and proposed the same split (views accessor as the write target, clones for the reader); this PR keeps `read_accept` as the views so the in-graph call site is unchanged and adds `snapshot_accept` for the reader.

## Accuracy / tests

- `test/registered/unit/spec/test_dspark_accept_tail.py::TestFoldedAcceptSnapshot` (CPU): the folded `accept_and_finalize` output must not alias the epilogue buffers and must keep its values after the buffers are rewritten. Fails on main (`AssertionError: True is not false : correct_len`), passes with the fix. The existing parity case still passes.
- `test/registered/unit/spec/test_dspark_overlap_readback_streams.py` (1-GPU): deterministic replay of the interleaving with real streams and `async_d2h`: a spin kernel on copy_stream stands in for the busy copy engine, forward_stream rewrites the buffers for step N+1; views read step N+1 (the hazard), the snapshot reads step N. On an H200 (main 5cbe2371a5 + this change): both cases pass; against the pre-fix `dspark_verify.py` the view case still reproduces the hazard and the snapshot case fails. The full `test/registered/unit/spec/` sweep passes (308 tests, 176 subtests). Re-run on 2026-10-19 against main 8e7601ae4a: same outcomes, sweep 311 passed, 182 subtests.
- Not reproduced end to end: the hang needs DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4 GPUs (TP4); @divyvasal validated the equivalent clone at 43.1M tokens per replica with 0 rank divergence in #42812.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation: not applicable.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results: not applicable (no numerics change; six tiny D2D copies per verify step).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+class TestFoldedAcceptSnapshot(CustomTestCase):

+            logits=logits,

+            gamma=STRIDE - 1,
+            verify_num_draft_tokens=STRIDE,
+            model_runner=None,
+            kv_injector=None,
+            tp_sync=_RecordingTpSync(),
+            verify_epilogue=epilogue,

+            target_logits=None,

+        self.assertEqual(accept.commit_lens.tolist(), [1, 3, 5])
+        expected = {
+            field: getattr(accept, field).clone() for field in accept.__struct_fields__
+        }
+        for field in accept.__struct_fields__:

@@ -0,0 +1,106 @@
+"""The DSpark accept readback must not race the next verify replay (#42465).
+
+Black-box mechanism: the folded accept writes fixed epilogue buffers that the
+next target-verify replay rewrites. The overlap scheduler issues the result
+readback (`accept_lens`, `next_token_ids`) on copy_stream after
+`copy_stream.wait_stream(forward_stream)`, then launches the next forward on
+forward_stream without waiting for the copy. When the copy engine is busy, for
+example behind HiCache write-through device-to-host traffic, the readback runs
+after the next replay and a view returns step N+1's values. Each TP rank races
+on its own, so ranks commit different token counts and deadlock.
+
+The interleaving is reproduced deterministically: a spin kernel on copy_stream
+stands in for the busy copy engine, so the readback always runs after the
+second rewrite. Views must observe the hazard (that is what the fix changes);
+the snapshot the folded accept now hands out must read step N.
+
+Run with:
+    python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/spec/test_dspark_overlap_readback_streams.py -v
+"""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.speculative.dspark_components.dspark_verify import (
+    DsparkVerifyEpilogue,
+)
+from sglang.srt.utils.common import async_d2h
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=15, stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small")
+
+BS, STRIDE = 4, 5
+FIELDS = (
+    "correct_len",
+    "bonus",
+    "cap_trim_lens",
+    "commit_lens",
+    "new_seq_lens",
+    "out_tokens",
+)
+# Long enough that the second rewrite on forward_stream always lands first.
+SPIN_CYCLES = 500_000_000
+
+
+class _StaticTpSync:
+    def sync(self, site, values):
+        return values
+
+
+def _epilogue(device) -> DsparkVerifyEpilogue:
+    return DsparkVerifyEpilogue(
+        max_bs=BS,
+        verify_num_draft_tokens=STRIDE,
+        device=device,
+        tp_sync=_StaticTpSync(),
+    )
+
+
+def _rewrite(epilogue: DsparkVerifyEpilogue, step: int) -> None:
+    """What a target-verify replay does to every accept buffer."""
+    for field in FIELDS:
+        getattr(epilogue, f"{field}_buf").fill_(step)
+
+
+def _readback_after_next_replay(handover: str) -> dict:
+    """forward_stream: replay N, (later) replay N+1; copy_stream: delayed readback."""
+    forward_stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    copy_stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    epilogue = _epilogue("cuda")
+    with torch.cuda.stream(forward_stream):
+        _rewrite(epilogue, 1)
+        if handover == "view":
+            outs = epilogue.read_accept(BS)
+        else:
+            outs = epilogue.snapshot_accept(BS)
+    # Scheduler._copy_result_to_cpu: the readback waits only for forward N.
+    copy_stream.wait_stream(forward_stream)
+    with torch.cuda.stream(copy_stream):
+        torch.cuda._sleep(SPIN_CYCLES)  # the copy engine is busy
+        host = {field: async_d2h(getattr(outs, field)) for field in FIELDS}
+    # The overlap loop launches forward N+1 without waiting for the copy.
+    with torch.cuda.stream(forward_stream):
+        _rewrite(epilogue, 2)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    return {field: sorted(set(host[field].flatten().tolist())) for field in FIELDS}
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(torch.cuda.is_available(), "needs a CUDA device")
+class TestDsparkOverlapReadbackStreams(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_views_read_the_next_replay(self):
+        # The hazard itself; if this stops reproducing, the test no longer
+        # exercises the interleaving the snapshot guards against.
+        seen = _readback_after_next_replay("view")
+        for field in FIELDS:
+            self.assertEqual(seen[field], [2], field)
+
+    def test_snapshot_reads_this_step(self):
+        seen = _readback_after_next_replay("snapshot")
+        for field in FIELDS:
+            self.assertEqual(seen[field], [1], field)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main(verbosity=2)
